claim: Reference implementation of a server-side toast queue in RSC: a Server Function writes a randomly-named toast-<uuid> cookie, a Server Component Toaster reads all of them each render, and a client component dismisses them with useOptimistic plus a Server Function that deletes the cookie.
quote: async function toast(message: string) { const cookieStore = await cookies(); const id = crypto.randomUUID(); cookieStore.set(`toast-${id}`, message, { path: "/", maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24, }); }

claim: The useActionState + useEffect toast pattern re-toasts stale messages on re-render unless the action's return value carries a timestamp/nonce compared against a ref.
quote: If the component re-renders, it might show an old toast message even if no new action was triggered.

claim: redirect() throws NEXT_REDIRECT, terminates rendering of the segment, serves a 303 when used in a Server Action, and must be called outside try/catch.
quote: Invoking the `redirect()` function throws a `NEXT_REDIRECT` error and terminates rendering of the route segment in which it was thrown. ... When used in a server action, it will serve a 303 HTTP redirect response to the caller.

claim: cookies() is async; .set/.delete are only legal in a Server Function or Route Handler (not during Server Component render); reading cookies opts a route into dynamic rendering; after a cookie write in a Server Function the UI is not unmounted but server-data-dependent effects re-run.
quote: HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a Server Function or Route Handler. ... The UI is not unmounted, but effects that depend on data coming from the server will re-run.

claim: useActionState returns [state, dispatchAction, isPending]; with Server Functions the initial state and payload must be serializable.
quote: const [state, dispatchAction, isPending] = useActionState(reducerAction, initialState, permalink?);

claim: 'use client' marks a module boundary: the module and its transitive imports are bundled and evaluated on the client, and props crossing the boundary must be serializable.
quote: 'use client' introduces a server-client boundary in the module dependency tree, effectively creating a subtree of Client modules.

claim: Developers report duplicate/stale toasts from useActionState + useEffect, and that a redirecting server action never returns changed state so success cannot be detected; proposed fixes include timestamps and awaiting the action promise directly instead of using useActionState.
quote: When server actions redirect, useActionState returns identical state values, preventing reliable success detection through state comparison alone.

claim: The three canonical ways to toast after a redirecting server action are useActionState + router.push, redirect with the message in searchParams, and redirect with the message in a cookie; the thread has no maintainer answer.
quote: Case 3: Cookie Pattern - Call the redirect function on the server, passing the desired message in a cookie, and create a component that listens to the cookie and displays the toast.

claim: Returning a JSON result and calling redirect() in the same server action are mutually exclusive; the recommended workaround is to set a cookie before the redirect and read it on the destination page to show the toast.
quote: set cookie before redirect, then read the cookie and show the toast accordingly

claim: Firing a Sonner toast from a useEffect produces two toasts under React StrictMode; the issue is closed as expected React dev-mode behaviour.
quote: useEffect(() => { const id = toast('count: ' + count); return () => toast.dismiss(id) }, [count])

claim: React Router 7's session.flash() writes a value deleted on first read; the action commits the session in the redirect's Set-Cookie header and the loader re-commits it; the docs warn that multiple nested loaders reading the same flash key causes race conditions.
quote: When using `session.flash()` or `session.unset()`, you need to be sure no other loaders in the request are going to want to read that, otherwise you'll get race conditions. Typically if you're using flash, you'll want to have a single loader read it, if another loader wants a flash message, use a different key for that loader.

claim: React Router community consensus: session flash is the reliable way to toast after a POST redirect; URL-parameter toasts re-fire on refresh, while flash messages self-destruct on read and so cannot double-toast.
quote: URL parameters: Refreshes can re-trigger toasts (unreliable)

claim: remix-toast is a server-side toast library for React Router v7 / Remix providing redirectWithSuccess-style helpers and getToast returning { toast, headers } for the root loader.
quote: essential utilities that you might need to show toast notifications to your users

claim: next-safe-action's useAction hook exposes onSuccess / onError / onSettled callbacks, letting a toast fire from the action result without a useEffect.
quote: const { execute } = useAction(myAction, { onSuccess: ({ data, input }) => { toast.success(`Created: ${data.name}`); }, onError: ({ error, input }) => { ... } });

claim: StrictMode re-runs effects (setup, cleanup, setup) an extra time in development only; production runs the effect once per mount.
quote: React's components will re-run Effects an extra time to find bugs caused by missing Effect cleanup.

claim: Hydration errors occur when the prerendered React tree differs from the first client render — the risk in toasts comes from server/client-divergent content (dates, locale), not from the empty toaster container itself.
quote: Hydration errors occur when there's a difference between the React tree that was prerendered from the server and the React tree rendered during the first render in the browser.

claim: next-safe-action provides end-to-end type-safe Server Actions with hooks, validation and callbacks for React/Next.js.
quote: End-to-end type safety ... Form Actions support ... Powerful middleware system
